ov: Five species of flightless bird found only in New Zealand, about the size of a chicken and the smallest ratites. Their wings are so small they’re hidden under hair-like feathers, and they smell prey through nostrils at the tip of the beak.

why.ac: Mostly nocturnal, perhaps because of predators, and it relies more on smell and touch than sight.

df: Prey it finds by smell, using the nostrils at the end of its long beak.
fx: Its closest relative is the extinct elephant bird of Madagascar, not New Zealand’s moa.
Four of the five kiwi species are listed as Vulnerable, mainly because of introduced predators.
